title: Caring for acrylic crochet
subtitle: How to wash and dry acrylic yarn projects to keep them looking new
excerpt: Acrylic is the most forgiving fibre to wash. It cannot felt and handles both machine washing and tumble drying. The main hazard is heat, which permanently alters the fabric.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book.

glossaryTerms.definition: A synthetic yarn made from polymer fibres. Machine-washable, widely available, and resistant to felting. Sensitive to high heat.

content.text: is the most low-maintenance crochet fibre. It does not felt, does not bleed dye after the first wash, and can be washed and dried repeatedly without deteriorating. The main thing to avoid is high heat: acrylic softens permanently above a certain temperature, losing its shape and elasticity.

Machine wash at 30 or 40 degrees C on a gentle cycle. Acrylic handles higher temperatures than this but lower temperatures extend the life of the fabric and preserve colour. A mesh laundry bag reduces pilling on textured stitches.

Tumble dry on a low or cool heat setting. High heat in the dryer can permanently alter the fabric's texture in the same way that steam blocking does, but without the controlled outcome. On a low setting, acrylic tumbles without damage.

Acrylic pills more than natural fibres under friction. Areas of heavy wear (under arms on sweaters, edges of blankets that get scrunched) develop small fibre bobbles. A fabric shaver removes these without damaging the underlying fabric. Reduce pilling in the wash by using a mesh laundry bag and a lower spin speed.

Do not iron acrylic directly. The heat will melt or permanently distort the fibres. If the piece needs blocking or flattening, use the steam-from-a-distance method described in the acrylic blocking guide: hold a steam iron above the surface without contact.

items.symptom: The piece feels limp and has lost its shape after drying
items.cause: The tumble dryer ran at high heat, which permanently softened the acrylic fibres.
items.fix: The change cannot be reversed. Dry future acrylic pieces on a low heat or air-dry setting only.

items.symptom: The fabric is heavily pilled after only a few washes
items.cause: The yarn is a low-twist acrylic with a fluffy surface that pills quickly under machine washing agitation.
items.fix: Use a mesh laundry bag and reduce the spin speed. For items that need to stay pill-free, hand wash instead.

content.text: Check the ball band care symbols before the first wash for any acrylic brand you have not used before. While most acrylic behaves as described here, blended yarns (acrylic mixed with wool or nylon) may have different care needs.
